title: General Aiptasia Husbandry Protocol
author: Pringle Lab
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.rkud4ww

steps.title: Set light conditions
steps.instruction: Provide 25 µmol photons mm⁻² s⁻¹ for symbiotic Aiptasia and 0 µmol photons mm⁻² s⁻¹ for aposymbiotic Aiptasia (kept in black containers). Use Philips F25T8/TL841 fluorescent lamps with a color temperature of 4100 K in the incubators.

steps.title: Prepare artificial seawater
steps.instruction: Mix artificial seawater (ASW) according to the Red Sea Coral Pro Salt manufacturer’s instructions using RO/DI water. Target salinity 32–34 ppt (checked with a refractometer) and pH ≈ 8.0. Prepare large batches in a 70‑gallon (265 L) barrel, pump for overnight mixing, check salinity next day and adjust with RO water or additional salt, then pump the water into a second 70‑gallon storage barrel. Install a filtration train (5 µm, 1 µm, 0.35 µm) between the barrel and the retrieval valves.

steps.title: Maintain temperature
steps.instruction: Keep stock cultures at 27 °C. Maintain spawning tanks at room temperature, between 22 °C and 27 °C.

steps.title: Store anemones in containers
steps.instruction: Place anemones in small plastic food storage containers (e.g., Cambro Camwear®). Avoid overcrowding. Use black containers for aposymbiotic animals to keep light out.

steps.title: Feed anemones with brine shrimp
steps.instruction: Feed anemones at least twice per week. Saturate each container with freshly hatched brine shrimp. Remove any uneaten food promptly to prevent water fouling; increasing feeding frequency can accelerate growth.

steps.title: Clean containers after feeding
steps.instruction: Wait at least 1 h (preferably > 3 h, but no longer than 8 h) after feeding before cleaning. Dump the water, being careful not to lose detached anemones. Use cotton swabs to remove algae from container walls while avoiding disturbance of anemones and pedal lacerates. If swabbing is unnecessary (especially for aposymbiotic cultures), simply dump and replace the water. Isolate any dying or unhealthy anemones and clean their water, checking for hypoxia, salinity, temperature, bleach contamination, or microbial buildup.

steps.title: Deep clean and sterilize containers
steps.instruction: Wash used containers with detergent and a brush until no biofilm is visible, then rinse with RO water. Soak in a 1 % bleach solution for ≥ 12 h, rinse thoroughly with DI water, run through a commercial dishwasher, rinse again with DI water, and air‑dry.

steps.title: Hatch brine shrimp eggs
steps.instruction: Fill a large hatching cone (≥ 6 L usable volume) with ASW and attach a bottom‑level air tube connected to an air pump. Add either 15 mL decapsulated eggs or 20 mL non‑decapsulated eggs. Turn on the air line and illuminate with a 100 W, 120 V T3 halogen bulb for the first 24 h to improve hatching rates. Maintain aeration to keep eggs suspended and rinse the cone sides with ASW as needed. Decapsulated eggs hatch in 24–48 h; non‑decapsulated eggs take longer. After hatching, turn off the air, allow unhatched shells to settle, open the drain valve, and collect shrimp with a fine net. Rinse shrimp briefly with fresh ASW, transfer to a 1 L cone of fresh ASW, then rinse the cone with RO water, brush the interior, and rinse again with DI water. Bleach the cone at the end of the week.

steps.title: Decapsulate brine shrimp eggs
steps.instruction: Place 600 mL DI water in a glass beaker, add 15 mL brine shrimp eggs, and aerate for 1–1.5 h while periodically swirling to keep eggs suspended. Add 300 mL chlorine bleach and continue aerating for 3–3.5 min, swirling constantly; eggs should turn brown‑orange (do not exceed 4 min). Strain the eggs through a shrimp net and rinse with DI water for 5 min or until the bleach odor is gone. The decapsulated eggs are ready for immediate use in the hatching cone or can be stored at 4 °C for later.

steps.title: Propagate via pedal lacerates
steps.instruction: Collect pedal lacerates produced by the culture and place them in fresh ASW. Allow them to develop into full polyps within a few days (never longer than one week).

steps.title: Propagate via cutting
steps.instruction: Using a sterile razor blade or scalpel, cut large anemones vertically through the oral disc into halves (or quarters with practice). Transfer the fragments to a container with fresh ASW, let them rest for 24–48 h until they re‑attach, then feed daily. Full regeneration occurs in ~1 week; newly formed tentacles require additional weeks to reach the size of the original ones.
